question: When you are confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do first and foremost?
choice_a: Flash your high beams at them
choice_b: Speed up to stay ahead of them
choice_c: Make every attempt to get out of their way
choice_d: Match their speed to hold your lane
explanation: The manual states that when confronted by an aggressive driver, you should first and foremost make every attempt to get out of their way.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.10.3, What You Should Do When Confronted by an Aggressive Driver

question: If you want to report an aggressive driver to the authorities, what information should you try to provide?
choice_a: Vehicle description, license number, location, and direction of travel
choice_b: The exact speed the vehicle was traveling
choice_c: Only the driver's approximate age
choice_d: The make and color of the vehicle only
explanation: The manual advises reporting aggressive drivers by providing a vehicle description, license number, location, and, if possible, direction of travel.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.10.3, What You Should Do When Confronted by an Aggressive Driver

question: According to the manual, what conditions encourage aggressive driving and road rage?
choice_a: Poor vehicle maintenance
choice_b: Heavy, slow-moving traffic and tight schedules
choice_c: Lack of driver training
choice_d: Bad weather conditions
explanation: The manual explains that heavy and slow-moving traffic combined with tight schedules leads drivers to take out their anger and frustration in their vehicles.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.10.1, What Is It?

question: Why is driving at night more dangerous than driving during the day?
choice_a: Headlights are prohibited on most highways
choice_b: Vehicles are required to travel faster at night
choice_c: Traffic laws change after dark
choice_d: Drivers can't see hazards as quickly and have less time to respond
explanation: The manual states that at night, drivers can't see hazards as quickly as in daylight, so they have less time to respond, making them less able to avoid a crash.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.1, It's More Dangerous

question: If your driver license says corrective lenses are required, what does the manual say about driving without them?
choice_a: It is allowed for trips under 10 miles
choice_b: It is allowed only during daylight hours
choice_c: It is illegal to move the vehicle without using corrective lenses
choice_d: It is allowed if a licensed passenger is present
explanation: The manual states it is illegal to move a vehicle without using corrective lenses if your license requires them, and recommends carrying a spare set.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors

question: About how far can a vehicle traveling 55 mph travel during even a brief two-second period of glare blindness?
choice_a: About one car length
choice_b: About two full football fields
choice_c: More than half the distance of a football field
choice_d: Less than 10 feet
explanation: The manual notes that even two seconds of glare blindness can be dangerous, since a vehicle going 55 mph will travel more than half the distance of a football field during that time.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors

question: According to the manual, fatigue impairs a driver's vision and judgment in a way most similar to which of the following?
choice_a: Alcohol and drugs
choice_b: Bright light, by causing temporary blindness
choice_c: Extreme heat, by causing dehydration
choice_d: Loud noise, by causing distraction
explanation: The manual states that fatigue, just like alcohol and drugs, impairs your vision and judgment.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors (Fatigue and Lack of Alertness)

question: About how many police-reported crashes per year does NHTSA estimate result from drowsy driving?
choice_a: 1 million
explanation: The manual cites an NHTSA estimate of 100,000 police-reported crashes a year resulting from drowsy driving.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors (Fatigue and Lack of Alertness)

question: According to the manual, at least what percentage of all heavy truck crashes involve fatigue?
choice_a: 5 percent
choice_b: 15 percent
choice_c: 75 percent
choice_d: 50 percent
explanation: The manual states that at least 15% of all heavy truck crashes involve fatigue.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors (At-Risk Groups)

question: Which of the following is listed in the manual as a warning sign of fatigue that means you should stop and rest?
choice_a: Trouble remembering the last few miles driven, or missing exits or traffic signs
choice_b: Feeling slightly hungry
choice_c: Needing to adjust the radio station
choice_d: Noticing the fuel gauge is low
explanation: The manual lists trouble remembering the last few miles driven, or missing exits or traffic signs, as a warning sign that you should stop and rest.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors (Warning Signs of Fatigue)

question: If you notice signs of fatigue while driving, what does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Stop driving and sleep for the night, or take a 15-20 minute nap
choice_b: Open the window and continue to your destination
choice_c: Turn up the radio and keep driving
choice_d: Drink coffee and continue driving for another hour
explanation: The manual advises that if you notice any signs of fatigue, you should stop driving and go to sleep for the night or take a 15-20 minute nap.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors (Warning Signs of Fatigue)

question: According to the manual, working more than 60 hours a week increases your risk of a fatigue-related crash by about how much?
choice_a: 90 percent
choice_b: 40 percent
choice_c: 5 percent
choice_d: 10 percent
explanation: The manual states that working more than 60 hours a week increases your fatigue-related crash risk by 40%.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors (Are You At Risk?)

question: About how often does the manual recommend taking a periodic break during a long trip to maintain alertness?
choice_a: Only once per full day of driving
choice_b: About every 500 miles or 8 hours
choice_c: About every 100 miles or 2 hours
choice_d: Every 25 miles or 30 minutes
explanation: The manual recommends taking periodic breaks about every 100 miles or 2 hours during long trips to maintain alertness.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.2, Driver Factors (Maintaining Alertness While Driving)

question: With low-beam headlights, about how far ahead can you typically see at night?
choice_a: About 100 feet
choice_b: About 1,000 feet
choice_c: About 500 feet
choice_d: About 250 feet
explanation: The manual states that with low beams you can see ahead about 250 feet, and with high beams about 350-500 feet.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.4, Vehicle Factors (Headlights)

question: When should you dim your headlights to avoid blinding other drivers?
choice_a: Only when a police officer signals you to do so
choice_b: Within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle within 500 feet
choice_c: Never, unless the other driver dims first
choice_d: Within 100 feet of an oncoming vehicle only
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to dim their lights within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle within 500 feet.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.11.5, Night Driving Procedures (Avoid Blinding Others)

question: What is the best advice the manual gives for driving in fog?
choice_a: Drive with your high beams on for maximum visibility
choice_b: Don't drive in fog; pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility is better
choice_c: Speed up to get through the fog bank quickly
choice_d: Follow closely behind another vehicle's taillights
explanation: The manual's best advice for driving in fog is not to drive at all, and to pull off the road into a rest area or truck stop until visibility improves.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.12, Driving in Fog

question: If you must drive in fog, what type of headlights should you use?
choice_a: Low-beam headlights and fog lights
choice_b: No headlights, to avoid reflecting off the fog
choice_c: High-beam headlights only
choice_d: Parking lights only
explanation: The manual advises using low-beam headlights and fog lights for the best visibility when driving in fog, even in daytime.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.12, Driving in Fog

question: Why does the manual warn against relying on the taillights of a vehicle ahead of you to judge where the road is when driving in fog?
choice_a: Following taillights is illegal in fog
choice_b: That vehicle may not actually be on the road at all
choice_c: Taillights are not visible in fog
choice_d: Taillights only work at night, not during foggy daytime conditions
explanation: The manual warns that seeing taillights or headlights in front of you may not be a true indication of where the road is, since the vehicle may not be on the road at all.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.12, Driving in Fog

question: What should you do with your flashers when driving in fog?
choice_a: Use flashers instead of headlights
choice_b: Use flashers only when passing another vehicle
choice_c: Turn on your 4-way flashers to give vehicles behind you a quicker chance to notice your vehicle
choice_d: Leave flashers off so you don't distract other drivers
explanation: The manual recommends turning on 4-way flashers in fog to give vehicles approaching from behind a quicker opportunity to notice your vehicle.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.12, Driving in Fog

question: According to the manual, should you assume that fog will thin out after you enter it?
choice_a: No, you should not assume the fog will thin out and should be ready to reduce speed
choice_b: Yes, fog is always thickest at its edges
choice_c: No, fog only forms during nighttime hours
choice_d: Yes, fog only exists in isolated patches
explanation: The manual explicitly warns not to assume that fog will thin out after you enter it, and to be ready to reduce speed.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.12, Driving in Fog

question: What is the minimum tread depth required in every major groove on the front tires for safe winter driving, according to the manual?
choice_a: 1/32 inch
choice_b: 4/32 inch
choice_c: 2/32 inch
choice_d: 8/32 inch
explanation: The manual requires at least 4/32 inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires (and at least 2/32 inch on other tires).
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.13.1, Vehicle Checks (Tires)

question: What does the manual say is a sign that ice may have formed on the road?
choice_a: An increase in traffic noise
choice_b: Excessive vibration in the steering wheel
choice_c: A lack of spray from other vehicles' tires
choice_d: A sudden drop in engine temperature
explanation: The manual states that a lack of spray from other vehicles indicates that ice has formed on the road.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.13.2, Driving (Check for Ice)

question: Why does the manual advise against using the engine brake or speed retarder on slippery winter roads?
choice_a: They wear out the brake pads faster than normal braking
choice_b: They can cause the driving wheels to skid on slippery surfaces
choice_c: They are illegal to use in winter conditions
choice_d: They make the engine overheat in cold weather
explanation: The manual warns not to use the engine brake or speed retarder on slippery surfaces because they can cause the driving wheels to skid.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.13.2, Driving (Adjust Turning and Braking to Conditions)

question: As the temperature rises to the point where ice begins to melt, what happens to the road surface?
choice_a: It has no effect on traction
choice_b: It becomes safe to resume normal highway speeds
choice_c: It becomes noticeably less slippery
choice_d: It becomes even more slippery
explanation: The manual notes that as the temperature rises to the point where ice begins to melt, the road becomes even more slippery, so drivers should slow down more.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.13.2, Driving (Adjust Speed to Conditions)

question: Why are exhaust system leaks especially dangerous in winter?
choice_a: They cause the tires to lose air pressure faster
choice_b: Carbon monoxide can leak into the poorly ventilated cab and cause drowsiness or death
choice_c: They make the defroster stop working
choice_d: They cause the radiator to freeze
explanation: The manual explains that exhaust leaks are especially dangerous when cab ventilation is poor, because carbon monoxide can leak in, causing sleepiness and, in large amounts, death.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.13.1, Vehicle Checks (Exhaust System)

question: What effect can driving through deep standing water have on your brakes?
choice_a: Water instantly improves brake stopping power
choice_b: Wet brakes can become weak, apply unevenly, grab, or cause a jackknife when pulling a trailer
choice_c: Wet brakes automatically dry themselves within seconds
choice_d: Wet brakes behave no differently than dry brakes
explanation: The manual explains that water in the brakes can cause them to be weak, apply unevenly, or grab, leading to lack of braking power, wheel lockups, pulling to one side, or jackknife.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.13.2, Driving (Wet Brakes)

question: After driving through deep water, what should you do to dry out your brakes?
choice_a: Pour water directly on the brake drums to cool them
choice_b: Maintain light pressure on the brakes for a short distance to heat them up and dry them out, then test stop
choice_c: Immediately apply the parking brake and leave it engaged
choice_d: Avoid touching the brakes at all for the next 10 miles
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to maintain light brake pressure for a short distance after crossing water to heat and dry the brakes, then make a test stop when safe.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.13.2, Driving (Wet Brakes)

question: In very hot weather, how often does the manual recommend inspecting tires?
choice_a: Every 30 minutes
choice_b: Once at the start and once at the end of the trip
choice_c: Only when a tire feels low
choice_d: Every two hours or every 100 miles
explanation: The manual recommends inspecting tires every two hours or every 100 miles when driving in very hot weather.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.14.1, Vehicle Checks (Tires)

question: If a tire is too hot to touch during hot weather driving, what should you do?
choice_a: Add extra air to the tire to compensate for expansion
choice_b: Continue driving slowly until the next stop
choice_c: Remain stopped until the tire cools off
choice_d: Let air out of the tire immediately
explanation: The manual instructs that if a tire is too hot to touch, you should remain stopped until it cools off, otherwise it may blow out or catch fire.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.14.1, Vehicle Checks (Tires)

question: Why does the manual warn against letting air out of hot tires to reduce pressure?
choice_a: The pressure will be too low once the tires cool off
choice_b: It will cause the tires to overheat further
choice_c: It is illegal under federal regulations
choice_d: It has no real safety effect either way
explanation: The manual explains that air pressure increases with temperature, and if you let air out while hot, the pressure will be too low once the tires cool off.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.14.1, Vehicle Checks (Tires)

question: Before removing a radiator cap on an overheated engine, what should you do?
choice_a: Pour cold water directly on the cap to cool it quickly
choice_b: Wait until the engine has cooled, since steam and boiling water can spray under pressure and cause severe burns
choice_c: Rev the engine to lower the coolant temperature
choice_d: Remove it immediately to release built-up pressure
explanation: The manual warns never to remove the radiator cap until the system has cooled, because steam and boiling water can spray under pressure and cause severe burns.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.14.1, Vehicle Checks (Engine Coolant)

question: In very hot or desert conditions, why does the manual advise going slowly enough to prevent overheating?
choice_a: High speeds create more heat for tires and the engine, increasing the chances of tire failure, fire, or engine failure
choice_b: High speeds cause the transmission to shift improperly
choice_c: Going slowly only improves fuel economy, with no safety benefit
choice_d: Slower speeds are required by law in desert regions
explanation: The manual explains that high speeds create more heat, and in desert conditions this heat can build up dangerously, increasing chances of tire failure, fire, and engine failure.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.14.2, Driving

question: What is a "passive" railroad-highway crossing?
choice_a: A crossing that is permanently closed to vehicle traffic
choice_b: A crossing only used by freight trains, never passenger trains
choice_c: A crossing equipped with flashing lights and gates
choice_d: A crossing with no traffic control device, where the decision to stop or proceed rests entirely with the driver
explanation: The manual defines a passive crossing as one without any type of traffic control device, requiring the driver to recognize the crossing and decide whether it is safe to cross.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.1, Types of Crossings

question: What does the round, black-on-yellow advance warning sign before a railroad crossing tell you to do?
choice_a: Speed up to clear the crossing before a train arrives
choice_b: Sound your horn continuously until past the tracks
choice_c: Slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks
choice_d: Change lanes immediately
explanation: The advance warning sign tells drivers to slow down, look and listen for the train, and be prepared to stop at the tracks if a train is coming.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.2, Warning Signs and Devices (Advance Warning Signs)

question: If there is no white stop line painted on the pavement at a cross-buck sign, how must a vehicle that is required to stop position itself relative to the nearest rail?
choice_a: No closer than 50 feet and no farther than 100 feet
choice_b: As close as possible without touching the rail
choice_c: No closer than 15 feet and no farther than 50 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Exactly 10 feet from the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states that, absent a stop line, vehicles required to stop must stop no closer than 15 feet nor more than 50 feet from the nearest rail of the nearest track.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.2, Warning Signs and Devices (Cross-buck Signs)

question: What should you do when the flashing red lights at a railroad crossing begin to flash?
choice_a: Proceed with caution since the crossing remains legal to use
choice_b: Only slow down if you can actually see a train
choice_c: Stop; a train is approaching and you must yield the right-of-way
choice_d: Sound your horn and continue across
explanation: The manual states that when the cross-buck's flashing red lights begin to flash, you must stop because a train is approaching and you are required to yield the right-of-way.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.2, Warning Signs and Devices (Flashing Red Light Signals)

question: At a gated railroad crossing, when should you stop?
choice_a: You should never stop; just slow down and proceed
choice_b: Only if a train is visible approaching
choice_c: When the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers across the road lane
choice_d: Only once the gate has fully lowered
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to stop when the lights begin to flash and before the gate lowers, remaining stopped until the gates rise and the lights stop flashing.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.2, Warning Signs and Devices (Gates)

question: Why does the manual warn "double tracks require a double check"?
choice_a: Double tracks are always located in high-speed zones
choice_b: A train on one track may hide a train approaching on the other track
choice_c: Double-tracked crossings require a different type of vehicle stop
choice_d: Double-tracked crossings never have working signals
explanation: The manual warns that a train on one track may hide a train on the other track, so drivers must look both ways and confirm no other trains are near before crossing.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.3, Driving Procedures (Double Tracks Require a Double Check)

question: About how long does it take a typical tractor-trailer unit to clear a single railroad track?
choice_a: At least 60 seconds
choice_b: At least 5 minutes
choice_c: At least 14 seconds
choice_d: About 2 seconds
explanation: The manual states it takes a typical tractor-trailer unit at least 14 seconds to clear a single track, and more than 15 seconds to clear a double track.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.5, Crossing the Tracks

question: What must you never do while your vehicle is actually crossing railroad tracks?
choice_a: Use your turn signal
choice_b: Check your mirrors
choice_c: Shift gears
choice_d: Maintain a steady speed
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs drivers not to shift gears while crossing railroad tracks.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.5, Crossing the Tracks

question: Which type of trailer does the manual specifically warn is at risk of getting stuck on a raised railroad crossing?
choice_a: A low-slung unit such as a lowboy, car carrier, or possum-belly livestock trailer
choice_b: A standard flatbed trailer
choice_c: An empty dry van trailer
choice_d: A tanker trailer under 5,000 gallons
explanation: The manual specifically warns that low-slung units such as a lowboy, car carrier, moving van, or possum-belly livestock trailer can get stuck on raised crossings.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.6, Special Situations

question: If your vehicle becomes stuck on railroad tracks, what should you do first?
choice_a: Stay in the vehicle and wait for the train to pass
choice_b: Attempt to push the vehicle off the tracks by hand
choice_c: Try repeatedly to drive the vehicle off the tracks
choice_d: Get out of the vehicle and move away from the tracks
explanation: The manual instructs that if you get stuck on the tracks, you should get out of the vehicle and away from the tracks, then call 911 and give the location.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.6, Special Situations

question: Before starting across a railroad crossing, what must you be sure of?
choice_a: That no other vehicles are behind you
choice_b: That there is a passenger in the vehicle
choice_c: That you can get all the way across the tracks before you start
choice_d: That your headlights are on high beam
explanation: The manual warns you should never let traffic conditions trap you on the tracks, and must be sure you can get all the way across before starting.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.15.5, Crossing the Tracks

question: On a long, steep downgrade, what should be the principal way of controlling your speed?
choice_a: The parking brake applied intermittently
choice_b: Coasting in neutral to save fuel
choice_c: The braking effect of the engine, using a low gear
choice_d: Continuous hard application of the service brakes
explanation: The manual states you must use the braking effect of the engine as the principal way of controlling your speed, saving your service brakes for when needed.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.1, Select a Safe Speed

question: When should you shift a manual transmission into a low gear before a downgrade?
choice_a: Before starting down the grade, not after speed has already built up
choice_b: Only once you feel the brakes starting to fade
choice_c: It doesn't matter, as long as you're in a low gear by the bottom
choice_d: Halfway down the grade, once you gauge its steepness
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to shift into a low gear before starting down the grade, since it is difficult or impossible to downshift safely after speed has already built up.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.2, Select the Right Gear Before Starting Down the Grade

question: What happens to brakes that become too hot from overuse on a long downgrade?
choice_a: They automatically reset to full stopping power
choice_b: They may start to "fade," requiring harder and harder application for the same stopping power
choice_c: They lock up completely and cannot be released
choice_d: They become more responsive the hotter they get
explanation: The manual explains that overheated brakes can start to fade, meaning you must apply them harder and harder to get the same stopping power, until eventually they may not stop the vehicle at all.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.3, Brake Fading or Failure

question: Why is it important to keep all of a vehicle's brakes properly adjusted, according to the manual?
choice_a: It is only a cosmetic issue, not a safety issue
choice_b: Adjustment only matters for the front brakes
choice_c: Improperly adjusted brakes use more fuel
choice_d: Brakes out of adjustment stop doing their share of the work first, causing the properly adjusted brakes to overheat and fade
explanation: The manual explains that brakes out of adjustment stop doing their share before those that are properly adjusted, which causes the other brakes to overheat and fade, reducing overall braking ability.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.3, Brake Fading or Failure

question: Using the manual's example, if your "safe" speed going down a grade is 40 mph, what is the proper braking technique?
choice_a: Apply the brakes at 40 mph to reduce speed to about 35 mph, then release, repeating as needed
choice_b: Apply the brakes only once, at the very bottom of the grade
choice_c: Hold the brakes continuously from the top to the bottom of the grade
choice_d: Never brake below 40 mph under any circumstance
explanation: The manual's example applies the brakes at 40 mph, reduces speed to about 5 mph below the safe speed (35 mph), then releases, repeating this cycle to the bottom of the grade.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.4, Proper Braking Technique

question: About how long should each brake application last when using the proper braking technique on a downgrade?
choice_a: Less than a quarter second
choice_b: About thirty seconds
choice_c: About ten minutes
choice_d: About three seconds
explanation: The manual states that the brake application in the proper downgrade braking technique should last for about three seconds.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.4, Proper Braking Technique

question: What is the purpose of an escape ramp on a steep mountain downgrade?
choice_a: To provide a shortcut that bypasses the downgrade entirely
choice_b: To weigh trucks for compliance with weight limits
choice_c: To safely stop runaway vehicles using a long bed of loose, soft material, without injuring drivers or passengers
choice_d: To allow vehicles to pass slower traffic safely
explanation: The manual explains that escape ramps are built to stop runaway vehicles safely, using a long bed of loose, soft material, sometimes combined with an upgrade.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.4, Proper Braking Technique (Escape Ramps)

question: What factors does the manual say determine the "safe" speed for a mountain downgrade?
choice_a: Only the posted speed limit on that road
choice_b: The total weight of the vehicle and cargo, length and steepness of the grade, road conditions, and weather
choice_c: Only the time of day
choice_d: Only the number of axles on the vehicle
explanation: The manual lists the total weight of the vehicle and cargo, the length and steepness of the grade, road conditions, and weather as the key factors in selecting a safe downgrade speed.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.16.1, Select a Safe Speed

question: According to the manual, why might steering away from an obstacle be safer than trying to stop?
choice_a: Steering is always safer regardless of vehicle type
choice_b: Brakes are less reliable than steering in every emergency
choice_c: You can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_d: Steering never requires as much space as braking
explanation: The manual states that stopping is not always the safest thing to do in an emergency, and that you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: Why should you avoid applying the brake while making a quick emergency turn?
choice_a: It causes the ABS system to disengage
choice_b: It's easy to lock your wheels while turning, which can cause you to skid out of control
choice_c: It has no meaningful effect either way
choice_d: Braking while turning improves steering response
explanation: The manual warns that it is very easy to lock your wheels while turning, and if that happens, you may skid out of control.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash (How to Turn Quickly and Safely)

question: What is "counter-steering" in the context of emergency steering?
choice_a: Using the parking brake to assist a turn
choice_b: Turning the steering wheel back in the other direction once you've passed the obstacle
choice_c: Turning the wheel as far as it will go in one direction only
choice_d: Braking hard while turning the wheel
explanation: The manual defines counter-steering as turning the wheel back in the other direction once you've passed the obstacle, treating emergency steering and counter-steering as one action.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: If you're forced to leave the paved road onto the shoulder in an emergency, what does the manual recommend regarding braking?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake immediately
choice_b: Never brake at all until you return to the pavement
choice_c: Brake as hard as possible immediately upon leaving the road
choice_d: Avoid braking until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake very gently
explanation: The manual recommends avoiding the brakes until speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then braking very gently to avoid skidding on a loose surface.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.1, Steering to Avoid a Crash (Leaving the Road)

question: What is the "controlled braking" method of stopping quickly?
choice_a: Braking only with the trailer brakes, never the tractor brakes
choice_b: Applying and releasing the brakes repeatedly at fixed 5-second intervals
choice_c: Using only the parking brake to stop the vehicle
choice_d: Applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, keeping steering movements small
explanation: The manual describes controlled braking as applying the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, while keeping steering movements very small.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.2, How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: What is the "stab braking" method?
choice_a: Braking only on the downhill side of a grade
choice_b: Applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock, then reapplying fully once the wheels start rolling again
choice_c: Tapping the brakes lightly and repeatedly without ever fully applying them
choice_d: Applying the parking brake in short, stabbing motions
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as applying the brakes fully, releasing when the wheels lock up, and reapplying fully as soon as the wheels start rolling again.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.2, How to Stop Quickly and Safely

topic: Brake Failure - Loss of Hydraulic Pressure
question: If you experience loss of hydraulic brake pressure and the pedal feels spongy or goes to the floor, what actions does the manual recommend?
choice_a: Steer directly into the nearest solid object to stop quickly
choice_b: Shift into the highest gear available
choice_c: Downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking/emergency brake
choice_d: Turn off the engine immediately while still moving
explanation: The manual recommends downshifting, pumping the brakes, and using the separate parking/emergency brake (while releasing it as needed to avoid wheel lockup) when hydraulic pressure is lost.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.3, Brake Failure

question: Which of the following is a major sign of tire failure listed in the manual?
choice_a: The engine temperature gauge suddenly reading cold
choice_b: The fuel gauge dropping rapidly
choice_c: A loud "bang" sound, heavy vibration, or the steering feeling unusually "heavy"
choice_d: The headlights flickering
explanation: The manual lists sound (a loud bang), vibration, and a heavy steering feel as the major signs of tire failure.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.4, Tire Failure

question: After a tire fails, what does the manual say you should do regarding the brakes?
choice_a: Pump the brakes rapidly the moment you notice the failure
choice_b: Apply only the parking brake, never the service brakes
choice_c: Slam on the brakes immediately to stop as fast as possible
choice_d: Stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down, unless you're about to hit something
explanation: The manual warns that braking when a tire has failed could cause loss of control, so you should stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed, then brake very gently.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.17.4, Tire Failure

question: What does ABS do that regular brakes alone do not?
choice_a: It always shortens your stopping distance
choice_b: It completely replaces the need for regular brakes
choice_c: It keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications
choice_d: It allows you to drive faster in bad weather
explanation: The manual defines ABS as a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications, activating only when wheels are about to lock.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.18, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten your stopping distance?
choice_a: Yes, ABS doubles normal stopping power
choice_b: Yes, ABS always stops the vehicle in a shorter distance
choice_c: No, ABS actually increases stopping distance in all cases
choice_d: No, it helps you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking but doesn't necessarily shorten stopping distance
explanation: The manual explicitly states that ABS does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.18, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after what date are required by the Department of Transportation to have ABS, according to the manual?
choice_a: January 1, 1990
choice_b: March 1, 1997
choice_c: March 1, 2000
choice_d: July 1, 1985
explanation: The manual states that truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, are required to have ABS.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.18.2, Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: If the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the startup bulb check or comes on while driving, what does this indicate?
choice_a: You may have lost ABS control on one or more wheels
choice_b: The vehicle has no brakes at all
choice_c: The vehicle is not roadworthy and cannot legally move
choice_d: The engine has overheated
explanation: The manual explains that if the malfunction lamp stays on after the bulb check, or comes on once underway, you may have lost ABS control on one or more wheels.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.18.3, How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: When only the tractor of a combination vehicle has ABS, what should you do if the trailer begins to swing out?
choice_a: Accelerate to straighten out the trailer
choice_b: Turn the steering wheel sharply toward the swing
choice_c: Immediately apply full brake pressure
choice_d: Keep an eye on the trailer and let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so
explanation: The manual advises that when only the tractor has ABS, you should keep an eye on the trailer and let up on the brakes, if it is safe to do so, if the trailer begins to swing out.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.18.5, ABS on the Tractor Only or Only on the Trailer

question: What is the exception to normal ABS braking procedure that allows a driver to fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop?
choice_a: Driving any vehicle with a full trailer, regardless of ABS
choice_b: Driving only on wet pavement
choice_c: Driving a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles
choice_d: There is no such exception under any circumstances
explanation: The manual notes one exception: if you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.18.6, Braking with ABS

question: If your ABS malfunctions but your regular brakes still work, what should you do?
choice_a: Stop driving the vehicle immediately and permanently
choice_b: Disable the regular brakes until ABS is repaired
choice_c: Only drive in reverse until it's fixed
choice_d: Drive normally, but get the ABS system serviced soon
explanation: The manual states that if your ABS malfunctions, you still have regular brakes; drive normally, but get the system serviced soon.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.18.7, Braking If ABS Is Not Working

question: Which of the following is one of the four causes of skids listed in the manual?
choice_a: Driving with underinflated tires only
choice_b: Using turn signals too early
choice_c: Over-braking, which locks up the wheels
choice_d: Using cruise control on the highway
explanation: The manual lists over-braking (locking the wheels), over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast as the four causes of skids.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.19, Skid Control and Recovery

question: What does the manual identify as the cause of most serious skids?
choice_a: Driving too fast for road conditions
choice_b: Following too far behind another vehicle
choice_c: Driving with headlights on during the day
choice_d: Using the parking brake at highway speed
explanation: The manual states that most serious skids result from driving too fast for road conditions.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.19, Skid Control and Recovery

question: In a rear-wheel drive-wheel skid caused by acceleration on ice or snow, what is the easiest way to stop the skid?
choice_a: Apply the brakes as hard as possible
choice_b: Turn the steering wheel sharply
choice_c: Take your foot off the accelerator
choice_d: Shift into a higher gear immediately
explanation: The manual states that acceleration skids usually happen on ice or snow, and taking your foot off the accelerator can easily stop them.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.19.1, Drive-wheel Skids

question: What is the first step in correcting a drive-wheel braking skid?
choice_a: Accelerate to regain traction
choice_b: Turn the steering wheel as far as it will go
choice_c: Stop braking, so the rear wheels can roll again
choice_d: Apply the parking brake fully
explanation: The manual instructs that the first step in correcting a drive-wheel braking skid is to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again and stops the sliding.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.19.2, Correcting a Drive-wheel Braking Skid

question: What is the only way to stop a front-wheel skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel sharply in the opposite direction
choice_b: Accelerate out of the skid
choice_c: Apply the parking brake immediately
choice_d: Let the vehicle slow down by easing off the brake and not turning or braking so hard
explanation: The manual states that when a front-wheel skid occurs, the only way to stop it is to let the vehicle slow down, easing off both turning and hard braking.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.19.3, Front-wheel Skids

question: What are the three basic steps to take at an accident scene, according to the manual?
choice_a: Protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured
choice_b: Move all vehicles immediately, call a tow truck, and leave the scene
choice_c: Take photos, exchange insurance information, and call your dispatcher
choice_d: Assess damage, file a police report, and contact your employer
explanation: The manual states that the basic steps at any accident are to protect the area, notify authorities, and care for the injured.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.20, Accident Procedures

question: When protecting an accident scene, where should you park if you are stopping to help?
choice_a: Away from the accident, since the immediate area will be needed for emergency vehicles
choice_b: In the same lane as the accident to warn other drivers
choice_c: On the opposite side of the road, facing oncoming traffic
choice_d: Directly behind the wrecked vehicles to block traffic
explanation: The manual advises parking away from the accident when stopping to help, since the area immediately around the accident will be needed for emergency vehicles.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.20.1, Protect the Area

topic: Accident Procedures - Caring for the Injured
question: What does the manual say about moving a severely injured person at an accident scene?
choice_a: Don't move them unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
choice_b: Always move them to the side of the road immediately
choice_c: Always move them into your own vehicle
choice_d: Move them only if they ask to be moved
explanation: The manual instructs not to move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.20.3, Care for the Injured

question: Which class of fire consists of wood, paper, and ordinary combustibles, extinguished by cooling and quenching with water or dry chemicals?
choice_a: Class D
choice_b: Class C
choice_c: Class A
choice_d: Class B
explanation: The manual's fire class chart lists Class A as wood, paper, and ordinary combustibles, extinguished by cooling and quenching using water or dry chemicals.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.21.3, Fire Fighting (Figure 2.20, Class/Type of Fires)

question: Which class of fire must NOT be extinguished with water, and instead requires non-conducting agents such as carbon dioxide or dry chemicals?
choice_a: Class B, gasoline and oil fires
choice_b: Class C, electrical equipment fires
choice_c: Class D, combustible metal fires
choice_d: Class A, wood and paper fires
explanation: The manual's chart specifies that Class C electrical equipment fires must be extinguished with non-conducting agents such as carbon dioxide or dry chemicals, and explicitly says DO NOT USE WATER.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.21.3, Fire Fighting (Figure 2.20, Class/Type of Fires)

question: Why should you not use water on an electrical fire?
choice_a: It can cause an electrical shock
choice_b: Water is only effective on Class D fires
choice_c: Water is flammable
choice_d: Water makes electrical fires burn hotter
explanation: The manual explains that water should not be used on an electrical fire because it can cause shock.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.21.3, Fire Fighting

question: Why should you not use water on a gasoline fire?
choice_a: It causes an electrical shock hazard
choice_b: It has no effect at all, positive or negative
choice_c: It will spread the flames
choice_d: It causes the fuel tank to explode instantly
explanation: The manual states that water should not be used on a gasoline fire because it will spread the flames.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.21.3, Fire Fighting

question: If you have an engine fire, what does the manual recommend regarding the hood?
choice_a: Remove the hood entirely before extinguishing the fire
choice_b: Pour water directly into the engine compartment first
choice_c: Don't open the hood if you can avoid it, and shoot foam through louvers, the radiator, or from underneath
choice_d: Open the hood immediately to let heat escape
explanation: The manual advises turning off the engine, avoiding opening the hood if possible, and shooting foam through the louvers, radiator, or from the vehicle's underside.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.21.3, Fire Fighting

question: Why should you keep the doors closed on a van or box trailer that has a cargo fire?
choice_a: It's required by law regardless of fire risk
choice_b: Closed doors automatically extinguish the fire
choice_c: Opening the doors supplies the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn much faster
choice_d: It prevents the cargo from getting wet
explanation: The manual explains that opening van doors on a cargo fire supplies oxygen and can cause the fire to burn very fast, especially with hazardous materials cargo.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.21.3, Fire Fighting

question: When using a fire extinguisher, where should you aim it?
choice_a: Directly into the center of the flames, as high as possible
choice_b: Wherever the smoke appears thickest, regardless of the flames
choice_c: At the source or base of the fire, not up into the flames
choice_d: At the ground several feet from the fire
explanation: The manual instructs to aim the extinguisher at the source or base of the fire, not up in the flames.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.21.3, Fire Fighting

question: About how much alcohol can the liver process per hour, according to the manual?
choice_a: About two ounces
choice_b: About one-third of an ounce
choice_c: The liver cannot process alcohol at all
choice_d: About one full ounce
explanation: The manual states the liver can only process about one-third of an ounce of alcohol per hour, considerably less than the alcohol in a standard drink.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving (How Alcohol Works)

question: What actually sobers up a person who has been drinking alcohol, according to the manual?
choice_a: Black coffee, if strong enough
choice_b: Only time, not black coffee or a cold shower
choice_c: A cold shower
choice_d: Physical exercise
explanation: The manual states that because the liver processes alcohol at a fixed rate, only time will sober you up, not black coffee or a cold shower.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving (How Alcohol Works)

question: According to the manual, which of the following drinks contain roughly the same amount of alcohol?
choice_a: A 12-oz beer and a 12-oz glass of wine
choice_b: A 5-oz shot of liquor and a 12-oz glass of wine
choice_c: Two 12-oz beers and one shot of liquor
choice_d: A 12-oz glass of 5% beer, a 5-oz glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-oz shot of 80-proof liquor
explanation: The manual states that a 12-oz glass of 5% beer, a 5-oz glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-oz shot of 80-proof liquor all contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving (What Is a Drink?)

question: What three factors determine Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC), according to the manual?
choice_a: The type of alcohol, the time of day, and the drinker's age
choice_b: The temperature of the drink, the container size, and the drinker's mood
choice_c: The drinker's gender, height, and eye color
choice_d: The amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it's consumed, and the drinker's body weight
explanation: The manual states BAC is determined by the amount of alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your weight.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving (What Determines Blood Alcohol Concentration?)

question: Why is it dangerous that alcohol first affects the part of the brain that controls judgment and self-control?
choice_a: It only affects vision, not decision-making
choice_b: It has no real effect on decision-making
choice_c: It causes immediate unconsciousness
choice_d: It can keep drinkers from realizing they are getting drunk
explanation: The manual explains that because judgment and self-control are affected first, this can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk, even though good judgment is necessary for safe driving.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving (Alcohol and the Brain)

question: At a BAC of .08, which the manual identifies as the drunk driving limit, what effects are described?
choice_a: Complete loss of consciousness
choice_b: No noticeable effect on driving ability
choice_c: Improved reaction time due to relaxation
choice_d: Definite impairment in coordination and judgment
explanation: The manual's BAC chart lists .08 as the drunk driving limit, with definite impairment in coordination and judgment.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving (Figure 2.23, Effects of Increasing Blood Alcohol Content)

question: Which of the following driving errors does the manual list as a common effect of alcohol impairment?
choice_a: Difficulty starting the engine
choice_b: Excessively cautious, slow braking at every intersection
choice_c: Overuse of turn signals
choice_d: Weaving, straddling lanes, and running stop signs or red lights
explanation: The manual lists straddling lanes, quick jerky starts, running stop signs and red lights, weaving, and improper passing as effects of alcohol impairment on driving.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.1, Alcohol and Driving

question: Under what circumstance does the manual say a driver may possess and use a drug prescribed by a doctor while driving?
choice_a: Only if the driver has a hazardous materials endorsement
choice_b: Only if the drug is taken before starting a shift
choice_c: If the doctor informs the driver the drug will not affect safe driving ability
choice_d: Prescription drugs are never permitted for CDL drivers under any circumstance
explanation: The manual states that possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor is permitted if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.2, Other Drugs

question: What does the manual say about mixing alcohol with other drugs?
choice_a: Combining small amounts of alcohol and medication is safe if taken with food
choice_b: Alcohol cancels out the effects of most drugs
choice_c: Only illegal drugs are affected by alcohol; prescription drugs are unaffected
choice_d: Alcohol can make the effects of other drugs much worse, so the safest rule is not to mix drugs with driving at all
explanation: The manual warns that alcohol can make the effects of other drugs much worse, and the safest rule is not to mix drugs with driving at all.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.2, Other Drugs

question: If you become too ill to safely operate a motor vehicle, what does the manual say you must do?
choice_a: Continue driving carefully at a reduced speed
choice_b: Not drive, except that in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place you can safely stop
choice_c: Have a passenger without a CDL take over driving
choice_d: Pull over and wait exactly one hour before continuing
explanation: The manual states that if you become too ill to drive safely, you must not drive, though in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place where you can safely stop.
source_note: Mississippi Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA 'Modernized Testing System' base content, Version: July 2017), Mississippi Department of Public Safety (DPS) Driver Service Bureau -- Section 2, Driving Safely, Subsection 2.22.3, Illness
